highlights.title: The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search
highlights.summary: New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times.
body: Google is trying to force Gemini on schools, and they’re not thrilled.

Many elected officials, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders, responded harshly, calling Google’s behavior “extortion.” Mamdani had recently announced a policy that barred 2-K-8 students from using AI in the classroom. In a statement to the Times, New York City schools chancellor Kamar H. Samuels said, “If Google doesn’t reconsider their position, we will explore other search options.” Chicago’s public schools have also reportedly told Google that if it can’t provide a version of Search without AI, “the district will look to other search solutions.”

Educators are wary of AI’s effect on students’ critical thinking skills, and some studies have shown that students who use AI generally perform worse on tests. There are also concerns about the mental health effects on children who develop relationships with chatbots at a young age. But Google is deeply embedded in classrooms across the US, which rely on Google Classroom, Chromebooks, and other services, and going fully Google-free might prove difficult.

highlights.title: GTA 6 Officially Cuts A Controversial Franchise Feature After 25 Years
highlights.summary: You can do anything you want in a Grand Theft Auto game, but the franchise has historically been defined by a handful of specific mechanics. Steal a car. Shoot pedestrians. And for better or worse, soliciting a prostitute.
body: Prostitutes made their debut as NPCs in 2001 with the release of Grand Theft Auto 3. These characters, which appeared on the game's streets at night, could be solicited by the player for $100. Though the encounters were explicit in nature, the animations at the time only showed the vehicle bouncing suggestively.

The arguably tame mechanic became infamous for two primary reasons. Many fans approach GTA as a chaos simulator, so players sometimes target sex workers indiscriminately. It became a running joke, for lack of a better word, for GTA fans to sleep with and immediately kill the women they hired. Once dead, the NPCs would drop the money the player used to hire them.

highlights.title: ‘Most extraordinary virtual world’: critics hail Grand Theft Auto VI as masterpiece
highlights.summary: Reviewers praise relationship between two leads in hotly anticipated release, whose trailer attracted 90m views in 24 hours. Good things clearly come to those who wait. After 13 years of anticipation, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here – and, according to critics, it’s a masterpiece.
body: The trailer for the video game, which returns players to Vice City, Rockstar’s fictional version of Miami, attracted more than 90m views in 24 hours when it was released in December 2023. Excitement continued to mount, with two release delays and a steady stream of leaks and speculation keeping the game in the headlines.

Now, Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at 99 out of 100 – tying with Nintendo’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record for the best reviewed video game since 1998.
In a five-star review, the Guardian’s Keza MacDonald said: “In GTA VI, Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have yet seen.”

MacDonald praised the fictional state of Leonida as an extraordinarily detailed world, populated by incidental encounters and activities that make it feel alive. But for all its violence and grotesque humour, what stood out was the relationship between Jason and Lucia – GTA’s first female protagonist.

And as part of her calming campaign, Kress has also been deploying a catchphrase that sounds like it was taken straight from the draft files of a summer of ’24 Democratic campaign strategist: “We’ve got this.”
“Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed. We’ve got this.”

“Our ambition will not change. Our passion to innovate will not change. Our commitment to customers, partners, and shareholders will not change. We thank you all for the great quarter that we had. Just remember, we’ve got this.”

But it's Wade, a three-time runner-up at the event, who is the form player of the pair leading into the last 16 matchup, having dropped only one leg across his two group-stage wins.

"It wasn't a good game at all," Van Gerwen, seeded 10th at the tournament, told Sky Sports after his victory over De Graaf.

highlights.title: The 10 greatest games to never get a GOTY nomination
highlights.summary: The Game Awards announced its 2026 nominations yesterday, though not without controversy. Grand Theft Auto 6 — a game that isn't even out yet — leads the pack with eight nominations, including Game of the Year.
body: While there's a lot to be said about 2026's Game Awards snubs, some of the greatest games of all time never received a GOTY nomination. While the games below may have been nominated (or won) in other Game Awards categories, they never got their fair shot at Game of the Year honors.

Dark Souls 3 was a gorgeous, somber conclusion to FromSoftware's groundbreaking Dark Souls trilogy. By speeding up the pace of combat, Dark Souls 3 bridged Bloodborne and Elden Ring, streamlining an already iconic gameplay loop. To close out its trilogy, FromSoft proved it had complete mastery over the gameplay style it innovated years earlier.

Despite widespread acclaim, Dark Souls 3 was not nominated for Game of the Year in 2016, only getting a nod for Best RPG. Fans should take comfort in the fact that 2016 was an absolutely stacked year, though, with Overwatch, Doom, and Inside all competing for top honors. There's also the fact that very difficult games face an uphill battle in the GOTY race.

highlights.title: Even His Own Officials Don’t Think Trump’s China Trip Will Lead to Progress on AI
highlights.summary: Fallout from the Nvidia scandal has made any negotiations around AI difficult, officials say.
body: Ahead of President Donald Trump ’s meeting with Xi Jinping on Thursday, administration officials privately tell Inner Loop they see little room for progress in alleviating AI safety and espionage concerns.

As he departed the White House, Trump left it an open question whether he would press Xi on Chinese interference in AI or the Nvidia scandal, as part of what officials say is an effort to not antagonize China during the summit.

But the fallout from former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed and suspected Chinese intelligence asset, has made any negotiations around AI development fraught for the world's two largest economies, officials say.

Back in September, the Trump administration moved to set up an AI incident hotline between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese vice premier He Lifeng to account for situations just like this one. Unfortunately, the communication channel remains at the concept stage and is not operational.

highlights.summary: Jermaine Wattimena was visibly emotional following his massive 10-8 win over Luke Littler in the last 16 at the Grand Slam of Darts, taking in the moment as the Wolverhampton crowd sang his name.
body: An English crowd chanting so heartily for a Dutch player is somewhat of a rarity, especially when they are taking on an Englishman, but it was the sensational manner of his victory over the world No 1 and back-to-back Grand Slam champion that won them over.
Littler was aiming for a Grand Slam three-peat after his wins in 2024 and 2025 but with the Dutchman prevailing, it is still only Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen who have achieved such a feat.
Wattimena led 3-2 before running away to get 7-2 up against Littler. He then held on as Littler fought back to 9-8 and pinned 77 on tops for what is now the biggest win of his career.
It was made all the sweeter given the fact Wattimena has felt the pain of a massive Littler comeback before. He was 7-2 up against 'The Nuke' at the Matchplay in 2025 before eventually being beaten.

body: The European Union has published a draft proposal for the DFA, calling for changes to in-game currencies to more clearly state their value, disclose loot box odds and give users ability to turn off loot boxes - with all IAPs disabled by default for minors.

Supercell has been a champion of the free-to–play mobile space since launching Hay Day and Clash of Clans back in 2012, making billions of dollars in the years since. It’s become one of the region’s most successful gaming companies.
Paananen said while the European Commission promises to protect consumers with new regulations, the opposite will happen.
He claimed that by making it harder for players to buy something, there will be fewer free games on the market. Around 95% of Supercell’s monthly players play for free.

highlights.summary: Newsmax filed an antitrust lawsuit on Thursday that seeks to block the Fox-Roku merger, arguing that the deal gives Fox unlawful monopoly power over the free streaming market. Fox Corp. closed the $22 billion acquisition earlier this month.
body: But in its lawsuit, Newsmax alleges that those commitments are unenforceable, and raises fears that Fox will deprive it of a key distribution channel.

“No single media company should have the power to determine which news voices Americans can see or hear,” said Christopher Ruddy, the CEO of Newsmax, in a statement. “Fox already dominates cable news and has repeatedly sought to undermine Newsmax as a competitor. highlights.title: America’s AI Chip War Is Heating Up in the Dumbest Possible Ways
highlights.summary: The Trump administration announced plans to clamp down on China’s access to AI chips. Apparently, the cheating scandal of the century was the motivation they were missing.
body: This week, the Trump administration made it significantly harder for Chinese companies to access some of the world’s most advanced AI chips. For years, tech firms like Alibaba and ByteDance could rent computing power from data centers overseas, allowing them to use powerful Nvidia chips they were generally prohibited from physically importing into China. This is known as remote access.

But under new plans announced on Monday, overseas data centers that want to provide large amounts of computing power to China will have to get special licenses and deal with other annoying new kinds of red tape. The White House also imposed stricter rules on shipments of advanced chips to five countries, including Singapore and Malaysia, where US officials suspect significant levels of smuggling may have taken place.

These are not new policy ideas, and similar proposals have been kicking around in Washington for a while. But the timing of Monday’s announcement is impossible to ignore. Yes, this is about Jensen Huang’s sex life.

The 680M is capable of running games like Fortnite and Minecraft at 1080p, and even more demanding games like Red Dead Redemption 2, Apex Legends, or even Cyberpunk with heavily modified settings.

highlights.title: Anorak raises $5m in pre-seed funding from Backed VC, Play Ventures, Supercell and MTG
highlights.summary: Interactive entertainment company Anorak has raised $5 million in pre-seed funding to develop games and experiences built around people's interests and hobbies. Founded by former Hutch CEO Shaun Rutland, Anorak will use the capital to support its 20-person team across London and Chengdu.
body: The company has not shared specific details of the products but plans to bring the playable formats to market and prepares to open its creator platform in early 2027.
The round was co-led by Backed VC and Play Ventures, with participation from Supercell, MTG and angel investors including Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron.
The idea came from Rutland's experience at Hutch, the London-based mobile game studio he co-founded in 2011 and led as CEO until 2025, before becoming executive chair.

“At Hutch, we learned just how passionate people can be about the things they love," said Rutland. “Car enthusiasts weren’t just playing our games; they were obsessing over every detail, sharing their knowledge and building communities around a common interest.

highlights.title: Elon Musk tries to explain what’s going on with Ukraine and Starlink
highlights.summary: Elon Musk said Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy is lying about disruptions to Starshield in Ukraine and that he's trying to misuse SpaceX's consumer service, Starlink, for military purposes.
body: The SpaceX CEO claims that Ukraine president Volodymyr Zelenskyy is ‘lying’ about using Starshield.

“From the beginning, I’ve said that Starlink is a civilian system,” Musk said. “It is not meant to be used for offensive drone strikes that kill people. If you want to do that, you need to do Starshield, which is a separate system that is controlled by the US government. But do not ask me as a private individual to make kill decisions.”

Musk also said that “if they want to do something that’s an offensive military action, it needs to be the Starshield system where the kill decision is that of the War Department, perhaps ultimately the president, and not mine.”

The interviewer, Andrew Ross Sorkin, said that President Zelenskyy refers to the system as Starshield and is claiming that is the system that was slowed down. “That’s false,” Musk said, claiming that Zelenskyy is “not always truthful.”

highlights.title: Missouri Basketball Dominates to Bounce Back With 61 Point Victory
highlights.summary: Missouri delivered one of its most dominant performances of the young season on Wednesday night, crushing Alcorn State 102-41 at Mizzou Arena. The Tigers controlled the game from the opening minutes, overwhelmed the Braves on both ends of the floor and secured a convincing 61 point victory.
body: The win moves Missouri to 4-1 on the season and gives head coach Dennis Gates’ team another opportunity to build momentum after its recent victory over Marquette. The Tigers also welcomed back an important contributor, as Mark Mitchell returned to the lineup after missing the previous game with a concussion.

The Tigers wasted little time establishing their dominance. Missouri opened the game with strong offensive execution, consistently finding opportunities around the basket while making life difficult for Alcorn State defensively.

The Braves struggled to find any rhythm, shooting poorly from the field and having difficulty dealing with Missouri’s size and athleticism. The Tigers took advantage of those struggles, creating separation through defensive stops, rebounds and transition opportunities.
Missouri carried a commanding 51-18 advantage into halftime. The 33 point lead reflected just how one-sided the opening 20 minutes had become.

Outside the airport, hundreds of protesters packed streets bearing signs — and at least one prop casket — saying “Trump out.” Others say “Reject Pax Silica,” the name for the US-led international initiative to secure chips and critical minerals used in the hardware fueling the AI boom.

highlights.title: 7 Best Shampoos for Hair Growth and Thickness, According to Dermatologists
highlights.summary: Can you use a shampoo for hair growth? Here, experts break down everything you need to know and we break down our favorite shampoo recs to get fuller and thicker hair.
body: I’ve been blessed with natural thick hair (thank you endlessly to my parents for passing along these genetics), but life happens and the effects of constantly being stressed, excessive hot tool use, and tight slicked-back ponytails are starting to manifest in a thinning hairline and some density loss. And I, like most people, have been wondering if all the shampoos that promise to help hair grow back are worth a spot in my hair routine.

The answer to that? It depends. If you’re wondering if these shampoos directly have anything to do with hair growing, then the answer, according to Y. Claire Chang, MD, board-certified dermatologist, is no. As Dr. Chang goes on to explain, hair growth occurs within the hair follicle, which is beneath the surface of the scalp. Since you are rinsing off shampoo, it only stays on your scalp and hair for a few minutes at best, which limits the amount of time that active ingredients have to interact with hair. “This is one of the biggest misconceptions in hair care,” she says. “Most shampoos marketed for hair growth may not actually stimulate hair growth.”

body: Congress is scrambling to provide legal recourse for deepfakes and online grooming.

On Tuesday, members of a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hosted a hearing calling for the end of forced arbitration for online harms. Their immediate target was Roblox, which they accused of evading legal complaints about children allegedly groomed on the platform by enforcing its own forced arbitration clause against users who agreed to the terms as minors, in some cases even under the age of 10. Separately, a few blocks away, Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) and Laurel Lee (R-FL) brought hotel heiress Paris Hilton to Capitol Hill to advocate for the Defiance Act, which would let victims of nonconsensual intimate deepfakes sue their creators.

The Ravens’ injury report does a disservice to their actual injury woes. Lamar Jackson has had a nightmare season in terms of injuries. They’re relying on newly acquired Cam Jurgens to center the offensive line after they lost several centers to injury over the first few weeks of the season. It turns out he just might not be any good anymore.

highlights.title: The LEGO Poké Ball Set Gets Its First Discount Ahead of Amazon's Black Friday Sale
highlights.summary: Amazon's Black Friday sale isn't going live until midnight tonight, but some of the best LEGO Pokémon deals have already been dropping early. That includes one of the most expensive sets in the entire theme, the giant LEGO Poké Ball.
body: This Poké Ball is more than just a really big LEGO display, it also houses some of the best minifigures and details from the franchise's 30-year history. The set's design is the classic spherical ball that operates on hinges so you can open it up to the scene inside. Inside the actual Poké Ball you get a miniature diorama recreating some iconic moments from the games. In the lid of the ball you'll see Professor Oak offering you a choice of three starter Pokémon, while the base features a Red minifigure battling a Picknicker's Eevee with Pikachu. At 2,386 pieces, this is an 18+ build that will take you a while to fully put together.

As far as LEGO Black Friday deals go, you're likely not going to see a better price than this any time soon. We expect Amazon to drop more discounts on sets tomorrow, but 20% off one of the most popular new sets of 2026 is going to be hard to beat at any retailer.

The official LEGO Black Friday sale doesn't actually start until actual Black Friday, which lands on November 27 this year. The LEGO Store will be hosting its annual Insider's Weekend event starting this Saturday, but that's more about loyalty points than straight discounts.

highlights.title: Four Maryland high school students sue after AI mistakes Doritos bag for gun
highlights.summary: Football players say they are ‘traumatized’ after being handcuffed and detained by police while waiting for rides home. Four current and former students at a Maryland high school have filed a lawsuit a year after armed police detained them, prompted by an AI alert that mistook a bag of Doritos for…
body: The plaintiffs sued Omnilert, the company behind the AI gun-detection system, Baltimore county police, the board of education, individual officers and the school principal, alleging unlawful detention and search because of technological and human errors.

“These students were failed not only by a technology that is prone to false alerts, but also by the very adults meant to keep them safe when we send them to school,” said Damon Hewitt, the president and executive director of the Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law, which is representing the students. “Instead of this protection, they were met with guns and traumatized. And it could have been even worse.”

The incident took place last fall. The students had just wrapped up football practice on the evening of 20 October when their coach passed out bags of Doritos to the team, according to the complaint. Taki Allen, a junior at the time, took several bags and was with his friends near the picnic tables waiting for their ride, when six local police cruisers emerged with lights flashing. Many officers unholstered their weapons and the students put their hands in the air, the complaint said.

highlights.title: This featherweight, flying robot carries its own sensors and computers
highlights.summary: The speedy microrobot flies without an attached motion-capture system, moving it closer to applications like agriculture or industrial surveillance.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."

Over the past decade, MIT researchers have developed aerial microrobots with bumblebee-like speed, agility, and durability, for tasks like precision agriculture or search-and-rescue. But these featherweight microrobots couldn’t carry the electronics needed for navigation, forcing them to remain connected to a motion-capture system in the lab.

Now, the researchers have designed a flapping-wing microrobot with onboard sensors and computation, which can follow a complex trajectory and land precisely on a sunflower outside the lab’s motion capture environment.
While the robot is still connected to an offboard power source, this demonstration highlights the potential of aerial microrobots to be used for precision agriculture in the future.
